summary: Evergreen Valley has launched a series of eco-friendly infrastructure projects, begun in earnest on September 8, 2023, with the goal of becoming a green neighborhood by 2030. Led by municipal managers, Dr. Linda Ferguson and Marcus Juarez, the projects cover solar power, green transportation, water conservation, community gardens, green building codes, green spaces, recycling and smart technology. Residents were engaged through public forums, and the town expects measurable reductions in emissions and resource use in the coming years.
one_line: Evergreen Valley is rolling out solar, transport, water, food, building, waste and smart-tech projects to become a green neighborhood by 2030.
key_facts: Evergreen Valley's eco-friendly infrastructure effort began in earnest on September 8, 2023, with the aim of transforming the neighborhood into a green utopia by 2030.
Sustainability expert Dr. Linda Ferguson (PhD in Environmental Science) and urban planner Marcus Juarez led public forums to educate residents and gather input.
Maria Vasquez, 58, became an active participant after attending the forums, saying "The choices we make now decide the future of our children."
Solar panel installation on public buildings began on November 15, 2023, spearheaded by Energy Committee chairperson Jonathan Green.
By January 5, 2024, the Evergreen Valley town council approved a bike share program and more lanes for bicycles and electric scooters.
The town's transportation vision includes a gradual transition to electric buses, which Marcus Juarez argued would significantly cut vehicular emissions.
A rainwater collection and recycling system in the public park was inaugurated on March 22, 2024, coinciding with World Water Day, and irrigates the park and other green spaces.
Beginning in spring 2024, vacant lots in Evergreen Valley were converted into community gardens for growing fruits and vegetables.
As of May 1, 2024, the building code requires all new construction to meet green criteria such as better insulation, natural lighting and energy-efficient appliances.
A comprehensive recycling program launched on July 10, 2024, expanding to cover electronic waste and composting, backed by educational campaigns and workshops.
Smart technology includes street lighting that adjusts to save energy and sensors that monitor air and water quality.

Reductions in carbon emissions and in water and energy consumption are expected to be quantifiable within a few years, and early evidence suggests greener neighborhoods lower stress and raise resident satisfaction.
